extracted.intended_audience: corporate SEC reporting professionals, corporate counsel, accountants preparing Form S-4/proxy statements for business combinations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what financial and interim statements (and related audit/reconciliation requirements) must be included in merger proxy statements and Form S-4 registration statements for targets and acquirers, and how thresholds (significance, resale status, registrant status, EGC status, etc.) affect those requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 303 MD&A requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 303 of Regulation S-K: management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as part of the information required in proxy/registration statements for business combinations; cited as a required disclosure alongside financial statements and other items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 304(b) accountant change disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 304(b) of Regulation S-K: disclosures of changes in and disagreements with accountants on accounting and financial disclosure must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a required disclosure element in proxy statements/Forms S-4 when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual-report-equivalent financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide financial statements that would be required in an annual report sent to security holders under Rules 14a-3(b)(1) and (b)(2) if an annual report were required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant’s security holders are not voting and transaction is not a roll-up, financial statements may be required depending on significance thresholds and other rules described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance-based requirement (>20%) for target financials
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company being acquired is significant to the registrant in excess of the 20% level (per §210.3-05(b)(2)), provide financial statements of the company being acquired for the latest fiscal year in conformity with GAAP; include earlier years if they were previously provided to target security holders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior years’ GAAP statements were distributed to target shareholders, include those years as well; the 20% test is applied per Rule 1-02(w). See examples 5.3.10/5.3.20 for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement when target significance ≤20%
rubrics_metrics.description: If the company being acquired is significant to the registrant at or below the 20% level, no financial information for the company being acquired need be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes pro forma and comparative per-share information when significance ≤20%, subject to aggregation rules for individually insignificant acquisitions (S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)(iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit practicability for latest fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements required for the latest fiscal year need be audited only to the extent practicable; prior-year statements need not be audited if they were not previously audited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant may request relief if an audit is impracticable; SEC staff will assess facts and actions taken to obtain a timely audit (see Question 5.3.150 and examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. GAAP reconciliation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If financial statements are prepared on a basis of accounting principles other than U.S. GAAP, provide a reconciliation to U.S. GAAP in accordance with Item 17 of Form 20‑F unless reconciliation is unavailable or unobtainable without unreasonable cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, provide a narrative description of all material variations in accounting principles, practices and methods between the non‑U.S. basis and U.S. GAAP when a reconciliation is not provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resale-by-underwriter audit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Form S-4 is used to register resales to the public by any person deemed an underwriter under Rule 145(c), the financial statements must be audited for the fiscal years required under Rule 3‑05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can increase the number of audited years required relative to a non-resale filing; see Question 5.3.120 and 5.3.140.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target entity determined by legal form of transaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of the target entity (the entity being acquired) is based on the legal form of the transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: in a reverse acquisition between two operating entities, the legal target’s financial statements are those required for Form S-4 even if the legal target is the accounting acquirer. (FRM 2200.1)

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquirer financial statement treatment (S-3 eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: An acquirer's financial statement requirements follow the same requirements as any 1933 Act registration statement; S-3‑eligible acquirers may incorporate required information by reference (Items 10–13 of Form S-4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non‑S-3 eligible acquirers must furnish the financial information with the Form S-4 (Item 14). Incorporation by reference can reduce duplication and effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include other acquisitions’ Rule 3-05 statements when applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: If the acquirer registrant has other consummated or probable acquisitions for which S‑X Rule 3‑05 statements would normally be required, those statements are included in Form S-4 to the extent not previously filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents omission of material acquired-business financial statements even if unrelated to the current target acquisition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of prior distribution to target shareholders on periods required
rubrics_metrics.description: If the target has previously provided its security holders with GAAP financial statements for earlier fiscal years, those earlier periods generally must be included on Form S-4 in addition to the latest fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show scenarios where prior distribution increases the number of years required even when other thresholds might reduce them (Examples 5.3.10 and 5.3.20).

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance + resale thresholds (20% and 40%) determine periods
rubrics_metrics.description: When registrant’s shareholders are not voting and the Form S‑4 will be used for resale: 20–40% significance generally requires latest fiscal year (or as determined by Rule 3‑05); >40% significance requires two most recent fiscal years; previously distributed additional years may also be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples 5.3.20 illustrate how 35% vs 45% significance and resale status change the number of years required.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-06 (9–12 month) exception not available
rubrics_metrics.description: S‑X Rule 3‑06 permitting financial statements covering nine to 12 months to satisfy a one‑year requirement does not apply to target company financial statements filed in a proxy statement or Form S‑4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception in Rule 3‑06(a) is available if the target changed its fiscal year; registrant may request permission from the Office of the Chief Accountant to apply Rule 3‑06 in other circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial information age requirements (registrant target)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the target is an SEC registrant, interim financial statements furnished must meet Reg S‑X age requirements (S‑X Rule 3‑12) — generally as of a date within 135 days (130 days for accelerated/large accelerated filers) of expected effective/mailing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim information must be as recent as the most recent Form 10‑Q filed; see Examples 5.3.30–5.3.40 illustrating staleness calculations and required interim periods (three vs six months).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim financial information for non-registrant target
rubrics_metrics.description: If the target is not an SEC registrant, furnish interim financial information of the target for the most recent period as would have been filed on Form 10‑Q had the target been a registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practically, this means including interim periods consistent with Form 10‑Q timing (see Example 5.3.30 scenarios).

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously acquired businesses (target's acquisitions) Rule 3-05 requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial statements for businesses recently acquired by or probable of being acquired by the target may be required on Form S‑4: if the target is an SEC registrant, file the Rule 3‑05 statements; if the target is not a registrant, include them only if omission would render the target’s financial statements substantially incomplete or misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination for non-registrants should be fact-specific considering significance of the acquisition to the target and timing (Question 5.3.100 and Example 5.3.50).

rubrics_metrics.name: EGC accommodation for target periods
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant is an emerging growth company (EGC), staff will not object to filing two years of the target’s annual and interim financial statements on a Form S‑4 in limited circumstances (if the registration constitutes its IPO of common equity or is filed after the IPO but before the next Form 10‑K), when the target is not an SEC registrant and registrant’s shareholders are voting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a narrow accommodation and applies only in the specified timing/filing situations (FRM 10220.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit requirements depend on target filing & resale status
rubrics_metrics.description: Audit requirements for target financial statements vary: if target is an SEC registrant, all years presented must be audited; if target is not an SEC registrant and the Form will be used for resale, audited years required per S‑X Rule 3‑05(b)(2); if not used for resale, audits required for years presented per 3‑05(b)(2) and latest year if practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether registrant’s shareholders are voting does not affect audit requirements. See Questions 5.3.120–5.3.140 and examples 5.3.60–5.3.70.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCAOB-registration not required for nonpublic-target auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Auditors’ reports for a nonpublic entity included in a proxy statement or Form S‑4 need not be issued by a PCAOB-registered firm and need not reference PCAOB standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if post‑consummation the target’s financial statements become the registrant’s (reverse acquisition), later filings (e.g., Form 8‑K) will require an auditors’ report issued by a PCAOB-registered auditor referring to PCAOB standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resale-by-deemed-underwriter increases audit scope
rubrics_metrics.description: If Form S‑4 will be used for resale by a deemed underwriter, target annual financial statements must be audited for the periods that would need to be audited under S‑X Rule 3‑05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Form will not be used for resale, only the latest year need be audited if the two prior years were not previously audited and audit of the most recent year is practicable (see Question 5.3.140).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining audit impracticability
rubrics_metrics.description: Determination that an audit is impracticable involves weighing feasibility and expense against usefulness to security holders; SEC staff will assess facts and actions taken to obtain the audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors considered include size/sophistication/relationships of owners, limitations obtaining an audit (e.g., closely held family business, significant inventory), and disproportionate financial cost (examples given). If relief is obtained, unaudited financial statements per Item 17 must still be furnished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closely held business determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether an entity is a 'closely held business' depends on facts and circumstances such as number and relationships of shareholders, trading activity, and whether shareholders are also employees/officers/directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation with legal counsel may be necessary; SEC staff may waive audit requirements for small closely held owner groups with access to information (Example 5.3.80).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bank reorganizing under newly formed holding entity — omission of operating bank financials
rubrics_metrics.description: An operating bank’s financial statements may be omitted from the initial Form S‑4 of a newly formed holding company if: (a) the holding entity is formed only to acquire the operating bank (satisfies General Instruction G), and (b) the operating bank separately furnishes US GAAP statements (need not be audited) for at least the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical disclosures for banks (Item 1400 Reg S‑K) may also be omitted under these conditions, but audited statements and required statistical disclosures must be furnished on the registrant’s first Form 10‑K for at least the two most recent fiscal years.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Instruction G and automatic effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Form S‑4 registration statements automatically become effective 20 days after initial filing if registrants mark the cover box asserting compliance with General Instruction G and meet all its conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To comply applicants must be registering shares of a holding company formed solely to acquire the stock of the organizing company and meet other Instruction G criteria; failure to check the box or meet criteria prevents automatic effectiveness though financial statements may still be omitted if SAB Topic 1.F conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAB Topic 1.F implications for bank filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the Form S‑4 is not automatically effective under Instruction G, financial statements may still be not required if all conditions of SAB Topic 1.F are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SAB Topic 1.F governs when financial statements and certain disclosures for reorganizations of banks may be omitted; see FRM 1150 and related guidance.
